title: Branches equally related by descent can differ greatly in amount of modification

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Branches equally related by descent can differ greatly in amount of modification

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A natural arrangement of groups must be strictly genealogical, but branches that are equally closely related to a common progenitor may differ greatly in how much they have been modified, and these differing amounts of difference are what is expressed by ranking them as different genera, families or orders.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I believe that the _arrangement_ of the groups within each class, in due subordination and relation to the other groups, must be strictly genealogical in order to be natural; but that the _amount_ of difference in the several branches or groups, though allied in the same degree in blood to their common progenitor, may differ greatly, being due to the different degrees of modification which they have undergone

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “Rules and difficulties in classification, explained on the theory of descent with modification”. Scope: all classes of organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-05: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Sister relationships, phenotypic disparity and rank are measurable with existing data. Different modification metrics limit universality but not the core prediction.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For sister clades of equal genealogical depth, compare morphological or molecular disparity and assigned Linnaean ranks. Frequent large disparity and rank differences among equally related branches support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Amount of modification has multiple legitimate metrics.

Morphological matrices are taxonomically selective.

fields.value:

data existence: 0.9

discriminating power: 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Unequal modification of sister lineages is directly measurable, and public trees make the sister-clade design straightforward for vertebrates. The genealogical 'must' in the same sentence is normative, so existing data test the empirical half. Morphological coverage is the main limit on adequacy, and the rate comparison itself is a standard phylogenetic analysis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For sister clades, which are equally related to their common ancestor, compare phenotypic disparity or morphological branch length and the Linnaean ranks later assigned to each side. The claim is confirmed if equally close branches often differ several-fold in accumulated modification, and refuted if sister clades are consistently similar in amount of change.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Molecular branch lengths are abundant, while the amount of bodily modification Darwin meant is available only where morphological matrices exist.

The requirement that a natural arrangement must be genealogical is a rule for classification, and datasets do not test the word 'must'.

Rank differences between sister clades partly record later taxonomic taste rather than a measured quantity of change.
